body.title: fix(sse): preserve empty event ids
body.body:
An SSE message with `id: ""` must send an empty `id` field so an EventSource client can clear its last event ID. The current truthiness check drops that field, leaving the previous reconnection cursor in effect. The [HTML SSE specification](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/server-sent-events.html#parsing-an-event-stream) defines an empty `id` value as resetting the last event ID.

Check whether the optional ID is a string so empty IDs are emitted and omitted IDs remain omitted. Wire-format regressions cover both a single message and an empty ID following a non-empty ID in a batch.

Validation on Node 24.21.0:
- Both new wire-format cases fail before the fix; all 53 SSE unit and integration tests pass after it.
- Lint, formatting, typecheck and `pnpm build` pass.
- The full unmodified test fixture run reports only the existing loopback IP expectation failure (`::ffff:127.0.0.1`); 3,037 tests pass, 51 skip after `pnpm build` (matching the CI build/test order). Applying the independent loopback test expectation locally allows the full suite to pass (3,038 passed, 51 skipped); that test-only change is excluded from this PR.

body.title: fix(cors): make stateful origin regex checks repeatable
body.body:
Reusing a global or sticky RegExp in the CORS origin array makes permission depend on its `lastIndex`. The same allowed origin can alternate between accepted and rejected requests, and checking an origin mutates the caller's regex state.

For these stateful regexes, check from index zero and restore the previous index in `finally`. Ordinary regexes keep their existing path. Regression cases cover both flags, repeated accepted origins, rejected origins and preservation of a pre-existing index.

Validation on Node 24.21.0:
- Both new regression cases fail before the fix; all 52 CORS unit tests pass after it.
- Lint, formatting, typecheck and `pnpm build` pass.

body.title: test: accept exact loopback addresses in fingerprint checks
body.body:
The Node fingerprint test fails on a dual-stack local listener when the peer address is `::ffff:127.0.0.1`. This is a valid loopback address, but the existing expectation accepts only `0.0.0.0` or `::1` (and does not anchor both alternatives).

Accept the exact loopback forms `127.0.0.1` and `::ffff:127.0.0.1` alongside the existing values, with the entire expression anchored. Arbitrary addresses and partial string matches still fail. No runtime behavior changes.

Validation on Node 24.21.0:
- The unchanged assertion reproduced one failure in `test/utils.test.ts` (197 passed).
- `pnpm test`: lint, formatting, typecheck and coverage passed; 3,036 tests passed, 51 skipped after `pnpm build` (matching the CI build/test order).
